usage: This is the standard greeting used from late afternoon until the end of the night. It is universally understood and used in both formal and informal contexts across Cairo. The phrase does not change based on the gender or number of people being addressed.

variants.label: warm and enthusiastic
variants.note: Add the vocative particle ya at the beginning to make the greeting sound warmer and more welcoming.

variants.label: affectionate
variants.note: Used with close friends or romantic partners as a flattering alternative.

variants.label: very casual slang
variants.note: A highly informal, slangy way to greet close friends, often accompanied by a hand gesture.

examples.arabic: مساء الخير يا جماعة، عاملين إيه؟
examples.transliteration: masa el kheer ya gama3a, 3amleen eeh?
examples.english: Good evening guys, how are you doing?

examples.arabic: مساء الخير يا فندم، أقدر أساعد حضرتك إزاي؟
examples.transliteration: masa el kheer ya fandem, a2dar asaa3ed 7adretak ezay?
examples.english: Good evening sir, how can I help you?

examples.arabic: مساء الخير، ممكن منيو المشروبات لو سمحت؟
examples.transliteration: masa el kheer, momken menu el mashroubat law sama7t?
examples.english: Good evening, could I have the drinks menu please?
